items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: I think around that time he was playing with Papa Celestan, no, Happy was playing with Celestan at that time.

ctx.x: Do you mean what they call, Zooty was playing what they call Memphis Time, was that it? Yeah, that's right. That's straight 4-4.

Yeah, straight 4-4 beat. Because when we played in New York, we had came when we was playing at the, oh I can't think of the name of the place, at the Palmont on Broadway. Oh yeah. It came by one night and came up and told me, see I kind of reminded him of the older days, you know? And uh, she had a beat with something similar to his, I said that's where I got it from you. Yeah. That's what's the way I got it from you. How about Sae in the early days? Well I didn't know nothing about Sae until around 47. Oh yeah,…

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: After we heard about what they had done to Papa Celestan's band, we didn't want to play down there anymore.

ctx.x: Where are all the places you've played all over the world? Where did you enjoy most?

Well, I'm going to tell you the truth, Tom. I enjoyed them all. I really did enjoy them all. I don't think one I did the other. But everywhere we went, we were treated royally. Nobody scorned us because we were what we are. Nobody overlooked us or nothing. They really enjoyed our playing. They enjoyed our company. And that was one thing that made me happy and actually that made us play better. Because we were treated like human beings. But you take like down and, well, I don't want to say it.
